newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: Taiwan still in talks with bidder for diesel sale.
newsitem.headline: Taiwan still in talks with bidder for diesel sale.

text.p: Taiwan's state-owned Chinese Petroleum Corp (CPC) remained locked in talks with the prospective buyer of its diesel cargo for July 23-27 lifting, free-on-board (fob) Kaohsiung basis, a CPC source said on Monday.
"We are now inclined to withdraw the award unless they accept our terms and conditions," a CPC source said. "(Otherwise) the deal is not attractive to us any longer."
The source said the offer was made at a "discount level" and CPC has sent a telex to the prospective buyer who need to confirm their acceptance based on the seller's terms and conditions.
The source declined to reveal what the terms and conditions were.
"The deal will be there if the winner has no objections to the terms and conditions," the CPC source said.
But so far the bidder has not yet accepted the conditions and "we are still discussing," the source added.

Market sources said the best bid for the 225,000-to-250,000-barrel cargo of 0.3 percent sulphur diesel was made by a Norwegian refiner at a 50 cents per barrel discount to Singapore spot quotes, fob basis.
When contacted a trader with the Norwegian firm said he would not comment on the tender award.
CPC had called for bids to be made on both fixed price and floating-price basis to Singapore spot quotes, instead of the usual fixed price only.
Prices in Singapore on a fob basis were in the range of $21.50-$22.00 per barrel.
In its last tender CPC sold two cargoes at $22.50-$23.00 per barrel, for July 2-8 lifting, fob Kaohsiung basis.
